newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey, Iran to renew oil import deal, boost ties.
newsitem.headline: Turkey, Iran to renew oil import deal, boost ties.

text.p: Turkey said on Friday it would renew a current oil import agreement with Iran and sign several deals to boost economic ties with its eastern neighbour amid efforts by the United States to isolate Tehran.
"In our talks with the Iranian delegation, we will conclude the renewal of the oil import deal, with effect from April," a senior energy official, who declined to be named, told Reuters.
"The new agreement will be for 4.5 million tonnes, like the current agreement which ends in April, or a little bit more than that," he said.
Turkey imports about 27 million tonnes of crude oil annually, most of which comes from Saudi Arabia.

Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani, accompanied by Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh, Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati and several other senior officials, have been in Turkey since Thursday for trade and political talks.
The visit marks a further step forward in strengthening ties between the two neighbouring Moslem countries since Necmettin Erbakan became Turkey's first Islamist prime minister in June.

The visit is likely to antagonise the United States, which is a close ally of NATO member Turkey and is trying to isolate Iran, which Washington accuses of sponsoring terrorism. Iran denies the charge.
Turkish officials said a series of agreements would be signed in Ankara on Saturday to boost trade and political ties between the two neighbours.

Agreements are likely to cover launching air transportation on Istanbul-Tabriz and Ankara-Tehran lines, rehabilitating a rail link from Tehran to the eastern Turkish city of Van and extending it as part of the historic "Silk Road" from China to Europe, among other things.
Officials said the two-way trade volume between the two countries would be doubled to $2 billion from 1997 when the agreements are put into practice.

Asked about a plan discussed at the meetings to launch a preliminary study for a pipeline to carry Iranian oil through Turkey, the energy official said: "The two sides only mentioned an intention. There is nothing tangible at this stage."

A Turkish official said on Thursday the two sides discussed launching a preliminary study to build a pipeline to carry Iranian oil to Western markets through Turkey's Mediterranean terminal of Ceyhan.
Iran and Turkey will build a pipeline to carry Iranian gas to Turkey from 1998 under a 23-year, $23-billion deal signed in August in Tehran.
The pipeline and gas deal was struck days after U.S. President Bill Clinton signed a law imposing sanctions on any company investing over $40 million a year in energy projects in Iran or Libya.
Ankara said the deal would not be affected by U.S. sanctions because Turkey was only constructing the stretch of pipeline on its own territory.
